{"body":"Part of #35 (section 2, ranked item 1).

## The defect

`TransformCollisionResolutionSystem` resolves every contact by **sweeping**: "moving from A toward B, at what fraction of the way do I hit?" — and places the body at that fraction. Correct for a body *approaching* a collider.

But a body can start the frame already **overlapping** one: knockback shoved it there, a spawner placed it there, or it clipped the corner of a large merged terrain rectangle. For an overlapping pair the swept solve returns a **negative contact time**, and following it hurls the body *through and out the far side* of the collider. Observed shipping *Witch v Necromancer*: knockback into the world-edge collider teleported the player clean out of the world, where it falls forever.

The intuition: if you find yourself inside a wall, you step out the **nearest face** — you do not rewind time along your velocity. Penetration is not a sweep.

## The fix (proven in the game, ready to port)

New `ResolvePenetration` path: when the boxes already overlap, translate the body along the **minimum-translation vector** (the shortest of the four exits). Strictly-touching-but-not-overlapping contacts still take the sweep, so resting contacts — the case sweeps exist for — are byte-for-byte unchanged.

Reference implementation: `roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj` → `Gmtk2026.Core/MonoDreams/collision/System/TransformCollisionResolutionSystem.cs` (the vendored module is at upstream HEAD `d0b94b0` baseline, so the diff is clean).

## Delivery

- [ ] Port `ResolvePenetration` + the overlap/sweep dispatch into `MonoDreams/collision/System/TransformCollisionResolutionSystem.cs`
- [ ] Carry the premises entry: **"Overlapping bodies depenetrate; only separated ones sweep"** (Why / Breaks / Tests structure), reworded to drop game-provenance lines
- [ ] Test: a body placed overlapping a collider exits by the nearest face (all four directions); a resting contact resolves identically to before; a normal approach sweep is unchanged

No API change. Behaviour changes only for the previously-broken overlap case.

**Value on its own:** any game with knockback, teleports, spawners or merged colliders has a "fell out of the world" bug waiting; this closes it.
","comments":[],"labels":[],"title":"collision: overlapping bodies must depenetrate along the MTV, not sweep"}

1	# collision — premises
2	
3	> Technical invariants the engine assumes about the collision module:
4	> `BoxColliderComponent`, `ConvexColliderComponent`, `ColliderTagComponent`,
5	> `IColliderComponent`, `CollisionMessage`, `ColliderBody`,
6	> `TransformCollisionDetectionSystem`, and the two resolution systems. Read this
7	> before changing any of those pieces or any system that emits or consumes
8	> `CollisionMessage`.
9	
10	## A collider IS an entity (colliders-as-entities)
11	
12	A collider is its own entity: a shape component (`BoxColliderComponent` or
13	`ConvexColliderComponent`) + its own `TransformComponent` (its pose, relative to a
14	parent body via the ordinary `ChildOf`/`Transform.Parent` hierarchy, or standalone)
15	+ an auto-applied `ColliderTagComponent`. The shape carries no embedded pose:
16	`BoxColliderComponent` is `{ Vector2 Size, ActiveLayers, Passive, Enabled }` and is
17	**centered** on the collider entity's `WorldPosition` with extent `Size` scaled by
18	`WorldScale` (rotation is intentionally ignored — the box stays axis-aligned; use a
19	convex for a rotated hitbox). `ConvexColliderComponent` keeps `ModelVertices` in the
20	collider entity's local space; `WorldVertices`/`BroadPhaseAABB` derive from that
21	entity's own `WorldMatrix`. `SATCollision.BoxWorldRect` is the single source of the
22	box's world pose (detection, resolution, debug outlines, and proxy geometry all route
23	through it).
24	
25	**Why:** the RFC's authoring-model fix — a collider authored off-center (a prefab
26	child, a feet-anchored footprint) places by moving/parenting the collider ENTITY, not
27	by an embedded offset that diverged authored-in-prefab vs placed-in-scene (the class of
28	bug PF-G patched). A flat scene where the collider sat at the entity's origin is
29	byte-identical.
30	**Breaks:** deriving a box world rect anywhere but `BoxWorldRect` (e.g. re-adding a
31	`Bounds` offset) reintroduces the offset divergence; putting two shape components on one
32	entity makes it a single collider entity with undefined shape (give each its own child
33	entity instead).
34	**Tests:** `MonoDreams.Tests/Collision/SATCollisionTests.cs` (box/convex world geometry,
35	centered box corners, child-entity world shape); `MonoDreams.Tests/Collision/ColliderEntityTests.cs`
36	(child-collider world shape under a moved/scaled parent).
37	**Depends on:** foundation — "`HierarchySystem` must run ahead of any system reading
38	WorldPosition"; foundation — "`WorldMatrix` is cached and computed lazily".
39	
40	## `ColliderTagComponent` tags collider ENTITIES and is the canonical query target
41	
42	`TransformCollisionDetectionSystem` queries by `ColliderTagComponent`, not by
43	`BoxColliderComponent` or `ConvexColliderComponent`. The tag is auto-applied (by the
44	detection system's component-added subscriptions) to any entity that gains either
45	collider component — under the entity model, that IS the collider entity.
46	
47	**Why:** the unification lets detection treat box and convex colliders through the same
48	query, dispatching to the right narrowphase test by type at iteration time. Two separate
49	queries would duplicate the broadphase loop.
50	**Breaks:** game code that adds `ColliderTagComponent` manually (or removes it while a
51	collider remains) desyncs the tag from collider presence. **The auto-tag is added on
52	the component-added event, so the detection system must be constructed BEFORE the
53	collider entities it should see** (or the entities re-add their collider) — a detection
54	system created after a collider entity never tags it, and the collider is invisible to
55	detection. The reference pipeline (and the tests) construct detection first.
56	**Tests:** `MonoDreams.Tests/Collision/ColliderEntityTests.cs` (the behavior tests rely
57	on detection-before-entities auto-tagging).
58	**Depends on:** —
59	
60	## Swept collision reads `TransformComponent.Delta`
61	
62	Dynamic collision tests (e.g., `DynamicRectVsRect`,
63	`DynamicConvexVsConvex` in `SATCollision`) read
64	`TransformComponent.Delta` to compute the entity's movement vector.
65	Correct `Delta` requires `TransformCommitSystem` ran for the previous
66	frame.
67	
68	**Why:** swept tests prevent tunneling — they check whether the movement
69	segment crosses the other collider, not just whether the endpoints
70	overlap.
71	**Breaks:** with a missing or stale `Delta`, fast-moving entities pass
72	through colliders. The bug is silent (no exception) and intermittent
73	(depends on speed).
74	**Tests:** none yet (the SAT primitives in
75	`MonoDreams.Tests/Collision/SATCollisionTests.cs` exercise the
76	narrowphase without going through a Delta-driven swept test).
77	**Depends on:** foundation — "`TransformComponent.Delta` is meaningful
78	only after `TransformCommitSystem` ran".
79	
80	## `ConvexColliderComponent.BroadPhaseAABB` must be refreshed when vertices change
81	
82	Detection's broadphase filters on `ConvexColliderComponent.BroadPhaseAABB`.
83	If the world vertices change (entity moved or rotated) without the AABB
84	being refreshed, the broadphase rejects an entity pair whose real
85	geometry would overlap.
86	
87	**Why:** the broadphase is an early-exit fast filter. Out-of-date AABBs
88	defeat the filter's purpose by producing false negatives instead of
89	false positives.
90	**Breaks:** a real collision is invisible to the broadphase and never
91	reaches the narrowphase — entities silently pass through each other
92	even though their actual shapes overlap.
93	**Tests:**
94	`MonoDreams.Tests/Collision/SATCollisionTests.cs::ConvexCollider_BroadPhaseAABB_UpdatedAfterTransform`
95	verifies the detection system's own update path keeps the AABB fresh.
96	A custom system that mutates vertices outside detection has no
97	protection.
98	**Depends on:** —
99	
100	## A collider's body is resolved via `ColliderBody.Resolve` (nearest RigidBody, else Velocity, else self)
101	
102	`ColliderBody.Resolve(collider)` is the one body-resolution primitive shared by
103	detection, resolution, and message construction. It walks the `ChildOf` chain up from
104	the collider entity (including the collider entity itself) and returns the nearest
105	ancestor carrying `RigidBodyComponent`; failing that, the nearest carrying
106	`VelocityComponent`; failing that, the collider entity itself. RigidBody wins outright
107	over a nearer Velocity (the `else` is a fallback, not a nearest-wins race). A standalone
108	collider — no physics ancestor — is therefore its own body: static geometry and trigger
109	zones reduce to collider == body.
110	
111	**Why:** a "body" is the physical thing a contact acts on; resolution write-back and the
112	swept movement delta belong to it, not to a collider child riding it. One shared helper
113	keeps detection/resolution/messages from each inventing a different answer.
114	**Breaks:** resolving to the collider child instead of the body corrects the wrong entity
115	(pre-mortem #1); a body query that stops at the first Velocity would pick a nearer
116	kinematic proxy over the real RigidBody.
117	**Tests:** `MonoDreams.Tests/Collision/ColliderEntityTests.cs` (the Resolve matrix:
118	standalone / RigidBody ancestor / Velocity ancestor / RigidBody-wins-over-nearer-Velocity /
119	plain-parent-falls-back-to-self).
120	**Depends on:** foundation — "`ChildOfComponent` and `TransformComponent.Parent` are two
121	intentional links"; physics — "`GravitySystem`/`VelocitySystem`" (the body markers).
122	
123	## Resolution corrects the BODY's Transform/Velocity, never the collider child
124	
125	The resolution systems apply the position correction (box: translate the body so its
126	collider's world centre lands at the swept contact point; convex/SAT: translate the body
127	by the MTV) and the velocity zeroing/damping to the **body** (`CollisionMessage.BodyA`),
128	read the shapes from the **colliders** (`ColliderA`/`ColliderB`), and read the swept
129	movement delta from the body's `TransformComponent.Delta`. The correction is a
130	world-space vector applied to a root body via `Translate`; for a root body world delta ==
131	local delta and the collider child follows via its parent's world matrix.
132	
133	**Why:** pre-mortem #1 — correcting a collider CHILD would drift it inside its parent
134	while the body sails on. The body is the mover; the collider only describes where it is.
135	A collider child's own local `Delta` is ~0 (it rides the body), so the swept test must
136	read the body's delta or it never sweeps.
137	**Breaks:** writing the correction to the collider entity de-syncs collider from body;
138	reading the collider's own `Delta` for the sweep starves fast movers of contacts. A
139	dynamic body that is itself a non-root child would need a world→local map for the
140	correction — the same interim limitation as before CE (documented, out of scope).
141	**Tests:** `MonoDreams.Tests/Collision/ColliderEntityTests.cs::Resolution_CorrectsTheBody_NotTheColliderChild`
142	(the child's local position is untouched while the body is blocked);
143	`MonoDreams.Tests/LevelEditor/IslandMilestoneTests.cs` (a player BODY with a CHILD collider
144	walks the island — the pre-mortem #1 tripwire).
145	**Depends on:** this file — "A collider's body is resolved via `ColliderBody.Resolve`";
146	foundation — "`TransformComponent.Delta` is meaningful only after `TransformCommitSystem` ran".
147	
148	## Multi-collider bodies are legal; resolution accumulates sequentially with re-validation
149	
150	A body may own N collider children (the former one-collider-of-each-type-per-entity
151	assumption is RETIRED — detection iterates collider entities, so it falls out naturally).
152	When two of a body's colliders both contact in one frame, resolution processes the
153	messages in contact-time order and each `Resolve*` **re-runs the narrowphase at the
154	current positions**: once an earlier correction has separated the body, the later
155	message's re-validation finds no penetration and no-ops. Sequential correction with
156	per-message re-validation is the accumulation rule — a body is never double-corrected
157	into an explosion.
158	
159	**Why:** the entity model makes multi-collider bodies trivial to author (a hitbox per
160	limb, a wide + a narrow footprint); the re-validation the resolver already did for a
161	single contact is exactly what keeps N contacts stable.
162	**Breaks:** applying every message's precomputed penetration blind (no re-validation)
163	double-counts overlapping corrections and flings the body.
164	**Tests:** `MonoDreams.Tests/Collision/ColliderEntityTests.cs::TwoColliderBody_BothChildrenContact_ResolvesWithoutExploding`.
165	**Depends on:** this file — "Resolution corrects the BODY's Transform/Velocity".
166	
167	## Reference physics pipeline order: Movement → Velocity → Detection → Resolution → Commit
168	
169	Each stage owns one job and the next depends on the previous stage's
170	output. The screen's pipeline assembler is responsible for registering
171	these five stages in this order. Skipping or reordering them silently
172	degrades collision quality.
173	
174	**Why:** Movement sets intent (game code writes `VelocityComponent`).
175	`VelocitySystem` applies intent to `TransformComponent.Position`.
176	`TransformCollisionDetectionSystem` finds contacts using the new
177	position + the previous frame's `Delta`. Resolution corrects
178	positions/velocities to honor contacts. `TransformCommitSystem` closes
179	the frame so next frame's `Delta` is meaningful.
180	**Breaks:** skip Commit → next frame's swept collision tunnels. Move
181	Resolution before Detection → resolution corrects against a stale
182	contact set. Mix gameplay position-writes with `VelocitySystem` → see
183	"`VelocitySystem` is the primary mover" in the physics module.
184	**Tests:** none yet (the integration tests exercise this order
185	implicitly —
186	`MonoDreams.Tests/IntegrationTests/InfiniteRunnerTests.cs::PlayerFallsOffLeftEdge`
187	depends on the full chain).
188	**Depends on:** physics — "`VelocitySystem` is the primary mover of
189	physics entities"; foundation — "`TransformComponent.Delta` is
190	meaningful only after `TransformCommitSystem` ran".
191	
192	## `TransformCollisionDetectionSystem` is single-threaded by design
193	
194	The detection system holds instance-level polygon buffers
195	(`_boxPolyBufA`, `_boxPolyBufB`). It is not thread-safe; only one
196	instance should be registered and invoked at a time.
197	
198	**Why:** the polygon buffers avoid per-collision allocations in the hot
199	path. Making them thread-local would re-introduce allocation pressure or
200	require an explicit pool.
201	**Breaks:** parallel invocations corrupt the buffers, producing nonsense
202	intersection tests — false positives, false negatives, or NaN-cascaded
203	entity positions.
204	**Tests:** none yet.
205	**Depends on:** —
206	
207	## One collider of each type per entity — RETIRED (colliders-as-entities)
208	
209	The former assumption (at most one `BoxColliderComponent` and one
210	`ConvexColliderComponent` per entity) is gone. A collider is its own entity, and a body
211	owns N collider children — see "A collider IS an entity" and "Multi-collider bodies are
212	legal; resolution accumulates sequentially with re-validation". Authoring two shapes on
213	ONE entity is still not a thing (that entity would be a single collider entity with an
214	ambiguous shape); give each shape its own child collider entity.
215	
216	## Layer-based filtering is the semantic pair filter
217	
218	Colliders with non-overlapping `ActiveLayers` sets are never tested
219	against each other. Layer membership is the "should these ever collide?"
220	filter that gameplay code uses to express groupings like "player vs
221	world", "player vs enemy", "projectiles vs everything".
222	
223	**Why:** layers express intent, not geometry. They are applied per
224	candidate pair *after* the spatial-grid broadphase has narrowed the
225	field by position (see "Broadphase is a uniform spatial grid"); together
226	they keep detection near O(n) for evenly distributed colliders rather
227	than all-pairs O(n²).
228	**Breaks:** a missing layer membership makes two colliders silently
229	not collide — the dev tunes the game logic for hours before realizing
230	the layer wasn't set.
231	**Tests:** none yet.
232	**Depends on:** "Broadphase is a uniform spatial grid".
233	
234	## Broadphase is a uniform spatial grid, and it is behavior-preserving
235	
236	`TransformCollisionDetectionSystem` narrows candidate pairs with a
237	uniform spatial grid rebuilt every frame, not an all-pairs sweep. Each
238	enabled collider's world AABB — **expanded by its BODY's
239	`TransformComponent.Delta`** (the collider rides its body; its own local delta
240	is ~0) — is bucketed into every grid cell it
241	overlaps, and only colliders sharing a cell are pair-tested (deduped on
242	the *ordered* pair). The grid changes performance, not results: it emits
243	exactly the `CollisionMessage` set the old all-pairs loop did. Two
244	properties make that hold: (1) inserting into *all* overlapping cells
245	means any two colliders whose AABBs overlap always share a cell, so no
246	real contact is pruned; (2) expanding by `Delta` means a fast mover
247	shares a cell with anything along its swept path, so the swept
248	box-vs-box test is never starved. The dedup key is ordered — (A,B) and
249	(B,A) stay distinct — so the symmetric double-message that resolution may
250	rely on is preserved.
251	
252	**Why:** all-pairs detection is O(n²) and stutters in the low hundreds of
253	colliders; the grid is ~O(n) for evenly distributed colliders (measured
254	~6× faster at 360 balls in the physics demo, and the gap widens with
255	count). Cell size adapts to the average collider AABB so small colliders
256	occupy ~one cell while the few large ones span several.
257	**Breaks:** bucketing by the un-expanded AABB lets a fast collider tunnel
258	(its swept path leaves the cells it was bucketed into) — the swept box
259	test silently misses contacts. Deduping on the *unordered* pair drops one
260	of the two symmetric messages, halving the impulse for resolvers that
261	expect both. Inserting into only one cell (e.g. the min-corner cell)
262	prunes real contacts whose colliders straddle a cell boundary.
263	**Tests:** behavior parity is covered indirectly — `SATCollisionTests`,
264	`InfiniteRunnerTests`, and `HeadlessDemoTests` pass unchanged after the
265	grid replaced the all-pairs loop.
266	**Depends on:** "Swept collision reads `TransformComponent.Delta`";
267	"`TransformCollisionDetectionSystem` is single-threaded by design".
268	
269	## Collision today couples to `TransformComponent` directly
270	
271	`TransformCollisionDetectionSystem` and the resolution systems read
272	`TransformComponent` by type — `TransformComponent.Position`,
273	`TransformComponent.Delta`, and `ConvexColliderComponent.WorldVertices`
274	(refreshed from `TransformComponent.WorldMatrix`). *Status:
275	implementation debt.*
276	
277	**Why:** the eventual end-state is loose coupling — collision against
278	any Transform-shaped contract — so a developer can swap in
279	`MyTransform` without re-implementing collision. The framework
280	doesn't enforce this today; the coupling is named here so the gap is
281	visible.
282	**Breaks:** a developer with `MyTransform` has to fork the collision
283	stack. The framework can't honestly call itself plug'n'play for
284	spatial substitutes until this loosens.
285	**Tests:** none yet.
286	**Depends on:** foundation — "Don't mix two Transform-shaped components
287	in one project".
288	
289	## `CollisionMessage` carries both collider and body granularities
290	
291	Detection emits `CollisionMessage` (or a custom message satisfying `ICollisionMessage` —
292	`TransformCollisionDetectionSystem` is generic via `CreateCollisionMessageDelegate`). The
293	message names FOUR entities: `ColliderA`/`ColliderB` (the collider entities — where the
294	shape and identity live) and `BodyA`/`BodyB` (the resolved bodies, via `ColliderBody`).
295	A is the initiator (the active, non-passive mover); B is the other side. Plus contact
296	point/normal/time, penetration depth, layer, and collision type. The delegate receives
297	all four entities, so a game classifier can key on identity (collider) or physics (body)
298	without re-walking the hierarchy.
299	
300	**Each consumer reads the side it needs (the pre-mortem #4 audit):**
301	| Consumer | side | why |
302	|---|---|---|
303	| resolution systems | `ColliderA/B` (shapes) + `BodyA` (write-back) + `BodyB` (touch msg) | geometry on the collider, correction on the body |
304	| `GameCollisionHelper` / runner classifier | identity, collider-first-then-body | "Player" rides the body, "Zone"/"Collectible" ride the collider |
305	| `ZoneDialogueTriggerSystem` | `ColliderB` | the zone's `DialogueZoneComponent` is on the collider entity |
306	| `RunnerCollisionHandlerSystem` | `BodyA` (player state), `BodyB` (dispose) | dispose the whole collectible/obstacle body, not a collider child |
307	| physics-demo `BallBounceSystem` | `BodyA` (write), `BodyB` (`FloorTag`) | collider == body there, so both resolve to the standalone entity |
308	
309	**Why:** identity and physics live on different entities now (a player's identity on its
310	body, its collider on a child; a zone's identity on the collider entity itself), so a
311	single "the other entity" field could not serve both dialogue zones and physics.
312	**Breaks:** a consumer reading the wrong side misses identity (a dialogue zone read via
313	`BodyB` when the body is a physics parent) or disposes/queries a collider child instead of
314	the game object; a custom message dropping a base field breaks resolution.
315	**Tests:** `MonoDreams.Tests/Collision/ColliderEntityTests.cs::CollisionMessage_CarriesColliderAndBody_ForBothSides`
316	(the message shape); `MonoDreams.Tests/Collision/CollisionConsumerAuditTests.cs` — the **completed
317	consumer audit** (CE-D, pre-mortem #4): each shipping consumer is wired and asserted to read the correct
318	side — `GameCollisionHelper` (identity collider-first-then-body), `ZoneDialogueTriggerSystem` (`ColliderB`,
319	+ a negative that it never falls back to `BodyB`), `RunnerCollisionHandlerSystem` (`BodyA` state / whole
320	`BodyB` dispose), `NPCInteractionSystem` (the collider-CHILD proximity path); the resolution systems are
321	covered by `ColliderEntityTests`, and the physics-demo `BallBounceSystem` (collider==body) by
322	`MonoDreams.Tests/IntegrationTests/HeadlessDemoTests.cs::HeadlessPhysicsDemo_…`. The milestone suites
323	(`IslandMilestoneTests`, `TriggerPlacementTests`, `PrefabMilestoneTests`) additionally exercise the
324	identity end-to-end through the real pipeline.
325	**Depends on:** this file — "A collider's body is resolved via `ColliderBody.Resolve`".
326	
327	## Colliders-as-entities perf is parity-or-better (RFC criterion)
328	
329	The entity model reads an already-computed `WorldMatrix`/`WorldPosition` per collider
330	instead of doing per-frame local-offset math, so it is expected to be parity-or-better —
331	the RFC's cache-hop concern applies only at scales this game does not approach. Coarse,
332	non-gating smoke measurement (in-process, one detection pass over 500 convex collider
333	entities, Debug build):
334	`ColliderEntityTests.PerfSmoke_ManyConvexColliders_OneDetectionPass_Completes` measured
335	**~0.3 ms** per pass. The test asserts only a generous 2000 ms ceiling (catches a
336	catastrophic regression, not a micro-regression).
337	
338	**Why:** the RFC gated CE on "no material perf regression"; this records the informal
339	number so a later change that regresses it is visible.
340	**Breaks:** a change that reintroduces per-collider per-frame allocation or an O(n²) pair
341	loop would blow past the ceiling.
342	**Tests:** `MonoDreams.Tests/Collision/ColliderEntityTests.cs::PerfSmoke_ManyConvexColliders_OneDetectionPass_Completes`.
343	**Depends on:** "Broadphase is a uniform spatial grid, and it is behavior-preserving".
344	
345	## Known limitations (acknowledged gaps)
346	
347	- **Tunneling at very high velocity** — swept collision prevents most
348	  tunneling, but at sufficiently extreme speed-to-collider-size
349	  ratios it can still occur. The only mitigation today is keeping
350	  gameplay velocities and collider sizes reasonable. *Velocity-cap
351	  safety net is on the backlog.*
352	- **Dynamic collider body that is itself a non-root child** — the resolution
353	  write-back applies a world-space correction to the body via `Translate`, which equals a
354	  local move only when the body is a root. A dynamic body nested under another moving/
355	  scaled/rotated transform would need a world→local map. No such case exists today (bodies
356	  are roots); documented as interim, same limitation as before CE.
357	
358	## Open questions
359	
360	- **`Passive` semantic (now documented, confirmed):** `Passive = true` means "does not
361	  INITIATE a collision" — a passive collider is never the resolver's moved body (it is
362	  never side A), but an active body IS resolved out of it, so passive static geometry
363	  BLOCKS while staying put (the `WallEntityFactory`/footprint/boundary idiom). Whether a
364	  passive collider reads as a physical blocker or a fire-only sensor is the game's
365	  `EntityInfoComponent` classification, not this flag.
366	- **`ColliderTagComponent` on disposal** — is it auto-removed when the collider component
367	  is removed, or only auto-added? (Auto-add is on the component-added event; there is no
368	  auto-remove.)
369	
370	## Aspirational direction
371	
372	- Loose coupling to `TransformComponent` so the collision stack works
373	  against any Transform-shaped contract.
374	- Velocity-cap safety net to prevent tunneling regardless of gameplay
375	  speed.
376	
377	## Follow-up debt
378	
379	The following premises currently have **Tests: none yet**:
380	
381	- Swept collision reads `TransformComponent.Delta`
382	- Reference physics pipeline order
383	- `TransformCollisionDetectionSystem` is single-threaded by design
384	- Layer-based filtering is the semantic pair filter
385	- Collision today couples to `TransformComponent` directly
386	
387	The `BroadPhaseAABB`, the colliders-as-entities model, body resolution, the write-back
388	rule, multi-collider bodies, the four-entity message, and the perf smoke now carry test
389	protection (`SATCollisionTests`, `ColliderEntityTests`, the milestone suites). The
390	pipeline-order premise is the highest-leverage remaining gap — an architectural test would
391	catch screens that omit `TransformCommitSystem`.

# collision — premises

> Technical invariants the engine assumes about the collision module:
> `BoxColliderComponent`, `ConvexColliderComponent`, `ColliderTagComponent`,
> `IColliderComponent`, `CollisionMessage`, `ColliderBody`,
> `TransformCollisionDetectionSystem`, and the two resolution systems. Read this
> before changing any of those pieces or any system that emits or consumes
> `CollisionMessage`.

## A collider IS an entity (colliders-as-entities)

A collider is its own entity: a shape component (`BoxColliderComponent` or
`ConvexColliderComponent`) + its own `TransformComponent` (its pose, relative to a
parent body via the ordinary `ChildOf`/`Transform.Parent` hierarchy, or standalone)
+ an auto-applied `ColliderTagComponent`. The shape carries no embedded pose:
`BoxColliderComponent` is `{ Vector2 Size, ActiveLayers, Passive, Enabled }` and is
**centered** on the collider entity's `WorldPosition` with extent `Size` scaled by
`WorldScale` (rotation is intentionally ignored — the box stays axis-aligned; use a
convex for a rotated hitbox). `ConvexColliderComponent` keeps `ModelVertices` in the
collider entity's local space; `WorldVertices`/`BroadPhaseAABB` derive from that
entity's own `WorldMatrix`. `SATCollision.BoxWorldRect` is the single source of the
box's world pose (detection, resolution, debug outlines, and proxy geometry all route
through it).

**Why:** the RFC's authoring-model fix — a collider authored off-center (a prefab
child, a feet-anchored footprint) places by moving/parenting the collider ENTITY, not
by an embedded offset that diverged authored-in-prefab vs placed-in-scene (the class of
bug PF-G patched). A flat scene where the collider sat at the entity's origin is
byte-identical.
**Breaks:** deriving a box world rect anywhere but `BoxWorldRect` (e.g. re-adding a
`Bounds` offset) reintroduces the offset divergence; putting two shape components on one
entity makes it a single collider entity with undefined shape (give each its own child
entity instead).
**Tests:** `MonoDreams.Tests/Collision/SATCollisionTests.cs` (box/convex world geometry,
centered box corners, child-entity world shape); `MonoDreams.Tests/Collision/ColliderEntityTests.cs`
(child-collider world shape under a moved/scaled parent).
**Depends on:** foundation — "`HierarchySystem` must run ahead of any system reading
WorldPosition"; foundation — "`WorldMatrix` is cached and computed lazily".

## `ColliderTagComponent` tags collider ENTITIES and is the canonical query target

`TransformCollisionDetectionSystem` queries by `ColliderTagComponent`, not by
`BoxColliderComponent` or `ConvexColliderComponent`. The tag is auto-applied (by the
detection system's component-added subscriptions) to any entity that gains either
collider component — under the entity model, that IS the collider entity.

**Why:** the unification lets detection treat box and convex colliders through the same
query, dispatching to the right narrowphase test by type at iteration time. Two separate
queries would duplicate the broadphase loop.
**Breaks:** game code that adds `ColliderTagComponent` manually (or removes it while a
collider remains) desyncs the tag from collider presence. **The auto-tag is added on
the component-added event, so the detection system must be constructed BEFORE the
collider entities it should see** (or the entities re-add their collider) — a detection
system created after a collider entity never tags it, and the collider is invisible to
detection. The reference pipeline (and the tests) construct detection first.
**Tests:** `MonoDreams.Tests/Collision/ColliderEntityTests.cs` (the behavior tests rely
on detection-before-entities auto-tagging).
**Depends on:** —

## Swept collision reads `TransformComponent.Delta`

`DynamicConvexVsConvex` in `SATCollision`) read
`TransformComponent.Delta` to compute the entity's movement vector.
Correct `Delta` requires `TransformCommitSystem` ran for the previous
frame.

**Why:** swept tests prevent tunneling — they check whether the movement
segment crosses the other collider, not just whether the endpoints
overlap.
**Breaks:** with a missing or stale `Delta`, fast-moving entities pass
through colliders. The bug is silent (no exception) and intermittent
(depends on speed).
**Tests:** none yet (the SAT primitives in
`MonoDreams.Tests/Collision/SATCollisionTests.cs` exercise the
narrowphase without going through a Delta-driven swept test).
**Depends on:** foundation — "`TransformComponent.Delta` is meaningful
only after `TransformCommitSystem` ran".

Detection's broadphase filters on `ConvexColliderComponent.BroadPhaseAABB`.

being refreshed, the broadphase rejects an entity pair whose real
geometry would overlap.

**Why:** the broadphase is an early-exit fast filter. Out-of-date AABBs
defeat the filter's purpose by producing false negatives instead of
false positives.
**Breaks:** a real collision is invisible to the broadphase and never
reaches the narrowphase — entities silently pass through each other
even though their actual shapes overlap.
**Tests:**
`MonoDreams.Tests/Collision/SATCollisionTests.cs::ConvexCollider_BroadPhaseAABB_UpdatedAfterTransform`
verifies the detection system's own update path keeps the AABB fresh.
A custom system that mutates vertices outside detection has no
protection.
**Depends on:** —

standalone / RigidBody ancestor / Velocity ancestor / RigidBody-wins-over-nearer-Velocity /
plain-parent-falls-back-to-self).

intentional links"; physics — "`GravitySystem`/`VelocitySystem`" (the body markers).

## Reference physics pipeline order: Movement → Velocity → Detection → Resolution → Commit

Each stage owns one job and the next depends on the previous stage's
output. The screen's pipeline assembler is responsible for registering
these five stages in this order. Skipping or reordering them silently
degrades collision quality.

**Why:** Movement sets intent (game code writes `VelocityComponent`).
`VelocitySystem` applies intent to `TransformComponent.Position`.
`TransformCollisionDetectionSystem` finds contacts using the new
position + the previous frame's `Delta`. Resolution corrects
positions/velocities to honor contacts. `TransformCommitSystem` closes
the frame so next frame's `Delta` is meaningful.
**Breaks:** skip Commit → next frame's swept collision tunnels. Move
Resolution before Detection → resolution corrects against a stale
contact set. Mix gameplay position-writes with `VelocitySystem` → see
"`VelocitySystem` is the primary mover" in the physics module.
**Tests:** none yet (the integration tests exercise this order
implicitly —
`MonoDreams.Tests/IntegrationTests/InfiniteRunnerTests.cs::PlayerFallsOffLeftEdge`
depends on the full chain).

physics entities"; foundation — "`TransformComponent.Delta` is
meaningful only after `TransformCommitSystem` ran".

The detection system holds instance-level polygon buffers
(`_boxPolyBufA`, `_boxPolyBufB`). It is not thread-safe; only one
instance should be registered and invoked at a time.

**Why:** the polygon buffers avoid per-collision allocations in the hot
path. Making them thread-local would re-introduce allocation pressure or
require an explicit pool.
**Breaks:** parallel invocations corrupt the buffers, producing nonsense
intersection tests — false positives, false negatives, or NaN-cascaded
entity positions.
**Tests:** none yet.
**Depends on:** —

The former assumption (at most one `BoxColliderComponent` and one
`ConvexColliderComponent` per entity) is gone. A collider is its own entity, and a body
owns N collider children — see "A collider IS an entity" and "Multi-collider bodies are
legal; resolution accumulates sequentially with re-validation". Authoring two shapes on
ONE entity is still not a thing (that entity would be a single collider entity with an
ambiguous shape); give each shape its own child collider entity.

## Layer-based filtering is the semantic pair filter

Colliders with non-overlapping `ActiveLayers` sets are never tested
against each other. Layer membership is the "should these ever collide?"
filter that gameplay code uses to express groupings like "player vs
world", "player vs enemy", "projectiles vs everything".

**Why:** layers express intent, not geometry. They are applied per
candidate pair *after* the spatial-grid broadphase has narrowed the
field by position (see "Broadphase is a uniform spatial grid"); together
they keep detection near O(n) for evenly distributed colliders rather
than all-pairs O(n²).
**Breaks:** a missing layer membership makes two colliders silently
not collide — the dev tunes the game logic for hours before realizing
the layer wasn't set.
**Tests:** none yet.
**Depends on:** "Broadphase is a uniform spatial grid".

## Broadphase is a uniform spatial grid, and it is behavior-preserving

`TransformCollisionDetectionSystem` narrows candidate pairs with a
uniform spatial grid rebuilt every frame, not an all-pairs sweep. Each
enabled collider's world AABB — **expanded by its BODY's
`TransformComponent.Delta`** (the collider rides its body; its own local delta
is ~0) — is bucketed into every grid cell it
overlaps, and only colliders sharing a cell are pair-tested (deduped on
the *ordered* pair). The grid changes performance, not results: it emits
exactly the `CollisionMessage` set the old all-pairs loop did. Two
properties make that hold: (1) inserting into *all* overlapping cells
means any two colliders whose AABBs overlap always share a cell, so no
real contact is pruned; (2) expanding by `Delta` means a fast mover
shares a cell with anything along its swept path, so the swept
box-vs-box test is never starved. The dedup key is ordered — (A,B) and
(B,A) stay distinct — so the symmetric double-message that resolution may
rely on is preserved.

**Why:** all-pairs detection is O(n²) and stutters in the low hundreds of
colliders; the grid is ~O(n) for evenly distributed colliders (measured
~6× faster at 360 balls in the physics demo, and the gap widens with
count). Cell size adapts to the average collider AABB so small colliders
occupy ~one cell while the few large ones span several.
**Breaks:** bucketing by the un-expanded AABB lets a fast collider tunnel
(its swept path leaves the cells it was bucketed into) — the swept box
test silently misses contacts. Deduping on the *unordered* pair drops one
of the two symmetric messages, halving the impulse for resolvers that
expect both. Inserting into only one cell (e.g. the min-corner cell)
prunes real contacts whose colliders straddle a cell boundary.

`InfiniteRunnerTests`, and `HeadlessDemoTests` pass unchanged after the
grid replaced the all-pairs loop.

`TransformComponent.Delta`, and `ConvexColliderComponent.WorldVertices`

implementation debt.*

any Transform-shaped contract — so a developer can swap in

doesn't enforce this today; the coupling is named here so the gap is
visible.

stack. The framework can't honestly call itself plug'n'play for
spatial substitutes until this loosens.

`TransformCollisionDetectionSystem` is generic via `CreateCollisionMessageDelegate`). The
message names FOUR entities: `ColliderA`/`ColliderB` (the collider entities — where the

- **Tunneling at very high velocity** — swept collision prevents most

  gameplay velocities and collider sizes reasonable. *Velocity-cap
  safety net is on the backlog.*
- **Dynamic collider body that is itself a non-root child** — the resolution
  write-back applies a world-space correction to the body via `Translate`, which equals a
  local move only when the body is a root. A dynamic body nested under another moving/
  scaled/rotated transform would need a world→local map. No such case exists today (bodies

- **`Passive` semantic (now documented, confirmed):** `Passive = true` means "does not

  `EntityInfoComponent` classification, not this flag.
- **`ColliderTagComponent` on disposal** — is it auto-removed when the collider component
  is removed, or only auto-added? (Auto-add is on the component-added event; there is no
  auto-remove.)

- Loose coupling to `TransformComponent` so the collision stack works

- Velocity-cap safety net to prevent tunneling regardless of gameplay
  speed.

`TransformCollisionResolutionSystem` resolved every box-vs-box contact by sweeping. A body that **starts the frame already overlapping** a collider (knockback, spawner placement, corner clip of a big merged terrain rect) got a negative contact time from the swept solve, whose "contact point" sits arbitrarily far back along the motion — proportional to the target's size — hurling the body through and out the far side (at a world edge: out of the world, falling forever).

`ResolveBoxVsBox` now checks `dynamicRect.Intersects(targetRect)` first: an already-overlapping pair is depenetrated along the **minimum-translation vector** (shortest of the four exits), zeroing velocity on that axis. `CollisionRect.Intersects` uses strict bounds, so strictly-touching contacts don't intersect — resting contacts take the sweep path byte-for-byte unchanged. Ported verbatim from the reference implementation named in the issue.

### 2. Companion fix the port surfaced: duplicate `[Subscribe]` double-resolved every message

The ported fix **did not hold** through the shipping `TransformPhysicalCollisionResolutionSystem`: all new tests initially failed with the body at the exactly *mirrored* coordinate (e.g. −210 instead of +210).

Root cause: the subclass re-annotated its `On` override with `[Subscribe]`. DefaultEcs's `IPublisherExtension.Subscribe` walks `DeclaredMethods` up the type hierarchy ([source](https://github.com/Doraku/DefaultEcs/blob/master/source/DefaultEcs/IPublisherExtension.cs)), so base + override annotations register the same virtually-dispatched handler **twice** — every `CollisionMessage` was resolved twice per frame. That hid indefinitely because the second pass is a zero-length no-op after a near-face swept block, but after a depenetration that exits *along* the motion, the swept re-solve back-projects the body clean across the target — reproducing the exact bug this PR removes. Verified empirically with a counting subclass (`published=1, handled=3` on a 3-level hierarchy) and at the DefaultEcs source level.

Two new entries in `MonoDreams/collision/docs/premises.md` (house Why/Breaks/Tests/Depends-on format):

- **"Each collision message is handled exactly once per resolution system"** — codifies the companion fix (workflow rule: new load-bearing invariant ⇒ propose the premise in the same PR).

- `OverlappingBody_ExitsByTheNearestFace` — `[Theory]`, all four exit directions.
- `REDACTED` — the knockback shape; under the old sweep this lands at −210 instead of +210.
- `TouchingBodyAtRest_IsNotDepenetrated_AndDoesNotJitter` — resting contact bit-identical across frames.
- `ApproachingBody_IsBlockedAtTheWallFace_SweepPathUnchanged` — normal approach still blocked at the face.

Every case fails if the override is re-annotated with `[Subscribe]`, so the companion premise is test-protected too.
